lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Independent application: building a fallback before committing

objective: Learners work through a fictional scenario where a character is relying on a single plan with no backup, build a concrete fallback (Plan B), and state the specific trigger condition that would tell the character when to switch to it, so they practice committing to a plan without being blindsided if it fails.
scenario: The learner reads a provided fictional scenario in which a character is relying entirely on one teacher to submit a single recommendation letter for a scholarship application with a fixed deadline, with no backup plan if it doesn't come through in time, and builds a concrete fallback with a specific switch-over trigger before the deadline arrives.
safetyNotes: The scenario is fictional and does not require the learner to name or rely on any real teacher, deadline, or application of their own.

tasks.directions: Before building a fallback, state Plan A and why the character currently believes it is enough.

prompts.text: What is the character's Plan A, and why does the character currently believe no backup is needed?

tasks.directions: List at least three specific things that could cause Plan A to fail, using the details given in the scenario.

prompts.text: I listed at least three specific ways Plan A could fail (not just 'it might not work').
At least one of my listed risks is something the character could notice before the deadline itself, not only on the deadline.

tasks.directions: Build a concrete Plan B and state the exact trigger condition that tells the character when to switch to it.

prompts.text: Describe the character's Plan B in specific terms, and state the exact trigger (a date, a piece of information, or an event) that should cause the character to switch from Plan A to Plan B.

tasks.directions: Consider why a stated trigger condition matters.

prompts.text: Why is deciding the trigger condition in advance different from just deciding 'I'll switch to Plan B if things don't work out'? What could go wrong without a specific trigger?

remediation: If the learner's Plan B is vague ('ask someone else') or the trigger condition is only a feeling rather than a specific date or event, reteach by requiring the fallback to name a specific alternative and the trigger to name a specific day or piece of information relative to the deadline given in the scenario.
extension: Have the learner identify a point at which even Plan B could fail, and sketch in one or two sentences what the character's next move would be if that happened too.
